messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High-severity: multiple containers on node ggpu-17 reported CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS and OOMs during serving. Auto-created incident thread. Please escalate if oncall.

alice_eng: seeing repeated container restarts on ggpu-17, started ~20:12 UTC. 3 distinct pods flapped within 2m, then a node-level OOM. stack traces show 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS' and a misaligned device pointer.

bob_sre: I'm oncall, pulling kube/node logs and coredumps. Can we cordon the node and shift traffic?

carol_runtime: yes, recommend cordon+drain. Also enable fallback to cpu-small model variant for affected routes while we triage. I'll push a routing policy to reduce batch_size.

bob_sre: cordoning ggpu-17 now: `kubectl cordon ggpu-17` -> done. Starting drain with graceful period 60s: `kubectl drain ggpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

alice_eng: logs from one of the runtime containers (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T20:12:24Z] runtime: token loop failed: nvml: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
traceback: serving/runtime/exec.cc:421: handle_step()
 kernel: smi_dump: pagewalk fault addr=0x7ffdeadbeef, misaligned_off=0x18
OOM-killer: invoked, process=runtime-worker pid=1442 rss=9.2G
```

carol_runtime: stack points to our kv-cache flush path + a recent hotpatch for continuous-batching. Hypothesis: race between async KV eviction and kernel pagewalk under high concurrent seq_len.

bob_sre: copying node dmesg for kernel team: `dmesg | tail -n50` shows: 
```
[ 24012.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 24012.346012] kernel: pagewalk: invalid pte at 0x7ffdeadbeef
[ 24012.346098] BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at ffff888012345678
```

kernel-team-bot: @bob_sre assigned to kernel-team, escalation ticket KT-5123 created. Please attach full vmcore and repro steps.

alice_eng: repro is intermittent. I can push a stress harness to one canary to reproduce an OOM + illegal access in ~10-20 minutes under heavy concurrent requests. Test plan: run continuous-batch workload with batch_size=16, kv-cache enabled, sequence_length=4096.

dave_support: any known customer impact? We have 2 high-volume customers on routes that prefer ggpu pool. One of them reported increased latency and a few 5xxs at 20:13.

emily_pm: need a short status for status.redwood.ai and a Slack customer update. Suggest: "We are investigating GPU node instability causing intermittent errors and higher latency for some customers. Mitigations in flight include routing to fallback capacity and node isolation. More updates in 30 minutes."

bob_sre: mitigation actions so far: cordoned ggpu-17, drained pods (most moved to ggpu pool a/b), enabled fallback route to dedicated-cpu-1, reduced default batch_size to 8 for canary traffic. Rolling restart on affected daemonset to pick older runtime build (revert hotpatch) as a precaution.

carol_runtime: rolled runtime back to v2.11.3 -> v2.11.2 on the canary set. Observing that the canary no longer triggers CUDA illegal access after rollback (15m). Still seeing OOM spikes in the drained node logs during repro.

bob_sre: node ggpu-17 is in maintenance; we are collecting vmcore with `crash` and uploading to KT ticket. ETA for kernel-team triage ~45m.

kernel-team-bot: kernel-team update: initial triage suggests a race in SMMU pagewalk + user pinned buffer eviction. Requesting the kernel's per-cpu pagewalk logs and a coredump of the driver. Assigning internal priority P1.

alice_eng: repro harness run 3/3 produced illegal_address at 20:31 on canary when batch_size bumped back to 16 and kv-cache enabled. With rollback and reduced batch_size we are stable.

dave_support: crafting customer message: "We've isolated the affected GPU node and routed traffic to fallback capacity. Some requests experienced elevated latency and occasional 5xx errors between 20:12–20:20 UTC. No data loss. We'll notify customers once full root cause is known." Any objections?

emily_pm: good. Post to status page and DM affected account reps. Add note: "If you have strict latency SLOs, consider enabling dedicated capacity until fix confirmed."

carol_runtime: follow-ups: we should add safer guards in KV eviction to avoid cross-thread pointer reuse, add an additional alignment check in the device pointer path, and add a churn detector to proactively reduce batch sizes under memory pressure. Filing runtime tasks RT-2044/RT-2045.

bob_sre: timeline for next update: 30m from now or on kernel-team update. For now, defining incident severity SEV2 (customer-facing but mitigated).

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity SEV2, mitigation=traffic-fallback/rollback/reduced-batching, owners=[alice_eng, bob_sre, kernel-team]. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.

alice_eng: thanks all — I'll stay on the thread to coordinate patches and QA. If kernel team requests a repro image, I'll hand over the canary harness and steps.

bob_sre: closing immediate mitigation: ggpu-17 remains cordoned and under investigation. Moving to postmortem prep once kernel-team confirms root cause.
